faqSchema.source:
Not necessarily. Fewer implants can sometimes support a bridge across a span. It depends on the number of teeth, the bone available and how the bite loads the area.

Generally several months, and longer where grafting is required. A staged timeline is provided at your planning appointment.

No. Placement, healing and restoration are separate stages. Where several implants are being placed, placement itself may be split across more than one visit depending on the case.

It depends entirely on the number of implants, whether grafting is needed and the type of restoration. You will receive a written, itemised plan before treatment begins.

No. Full-arch implant treatment is not currently offered here.

It can happen, and how it is managed depends on the design of the restoration and the reason for the failure. This is discussed as part of your planning so you understand the risks before committing.

fields.value: Dental Implants

fields.label: Main heading
fields.value: Replacing several teeth in a row.

fields.label: Introduction
fields.value: Where more than one tooth is missing, implants can be used in two ways: an implant and crown for each missing tooth, or fewer implants supporting a bridge across the span.

fields.label: Introduction
fields.value: Which approach suits depends on how many teeth are missing, where they are, how much bone is available, your bite and your budget. Two implants supporting a three-unit bridge, for example, can replace three teeth without needing a third implant, provided the bone and the loading are right.

fields.label: Small heading
fields.value: Assessment and planning

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Multi-implant cases require more planning than a single implant, because implant position, spacing and angulation all have to work together and with the finished restoration.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Planning starts with an examination of the remaining teeth, gums and bite, followed by 3D CBCT imaging to map bone volume and the position of nerves and sinuses across the whole area. From that, Dr Meg works out how many implants are needed, where they should sit and what the finished restoration should look like — before anything is placed.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Where bone volume is insufficient, grafting may be required first, and that is factored into the plan and the timeline from the beginning.

fields.label: Small heading
fields.value: Staged treatment and staged cost

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Treatment of this kind runs over months, and the cost is significant. You will be given a written plan setting out the stages, the timeline and the cost of each stage before anything begins, so there are no surprises partway through.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Dr Meg places and restores implants herself, so the same clinician sees the case from planning through to the final restoration.

fields.label: Small heading
fields.value: What we do not offer

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: All-on-4 and full-arch implant treatment is not provided at Lava Street Dental. Where that is what you need, we will discuss alternatives or refer you.

fields.label: Small heading
fields.value: Alternatives worth considering

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Implants are not always the right answer, and cost is a legitimate factor. A partial denture replaces multiple missing teeth without surgery at considerably lower cost, and a conventional bridge may suit where the neighbouring teeth need crowning anyway. Dr Meg will lay out the realistic options rather than presenting implants as the only one.

fields.label: Small heading
fields.value: Maintenance

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Implant-supported restorations need daily cleaning underneath and around, and regular professional maintenance. The gum and bone around an implant can become inflamed and recede — peri-implantitis — and it is the main reason implant restorations fail over time. We will show you the cleaning technique and check it at every visit.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently asked questions

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: Do I need one implant per missing tooth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Not necessarily. Fewer implants can sometimes support a bridge across a span. It depends on the number of teeth, the bone available and how the bite loads the area.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: How long does treatment take?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Generally several months, and longer where grafting is required. A staged timeline is provided at your planning appointment.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: Is it done all in one appointment?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Placement, healing and restoration are separate stages. Where several implants are being placed, placement itself may be split across more than one visit depending on the case.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: How much does it cost?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It depends entirely on the number of implants, whether grafting is needed and the type of restoration. You will receive a written, itemised plan before treatment begins.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: Do you offer All-on-4?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Full-arch implant treatment is not currently offered here.

fields.label: Button words
fields.value: What if one implant fails?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It can happen, and how it is managed depends on the design of the restoration and the reason for the failure. This is discussed as part of your planning so you understand the risks before committing.
